description_ru: Сэм смотрит две квартиры с агентом, сравнивает цену, этаж и вид и подписывает договор. Лексика аренды жилья.
text:
Helen: Good morning, Mr Parker. I am Helen Hill from Brightside Homes. Did you have trouble finding the building?
Sam: Good morning. No, it was easy. I took the bus, and the stop is right in front of the door.
Helen: Excellent. That is one of the advantages of this street. Shall we see the first flat?
Sam: Yes, please. How many rooms does it have?
Helen: It has two bedrooms, a living room, a small kitchen and a bathroom. It is on the third floor.
Sam: Is there a lift?
Helen: I am afraid not. But the stairs are wide and clean, and the neighbours are friendly.
Sam: Hmm. I carry a lot of heavy boxes for my work. Stairs could be a problem.
Helen: I understand. Let us look at the flat first. Please come in.
Sam: Oh, this is lovely. The living room is bigger than I expected.
Helen: Yes, and look at the window. In the afternoon you get a lot of sun.
Sam: The kitchen is quite small, though. Where would I put a table?
Helen: You can put a small table in the living room, near the window. Many people do that.
Sam: And how much is the rent?
Helen: It is nine hundred pounds a month, and the bills are not included.
Sam: That is more expensive than I wanted. My limit is eight hundred.
Helen: Then I recommend the second flat. It is in the same area, but it is cheaper.
Sam: Is it as nice as this one?
Helen: It is smaller, but it has a balcony and a lift. And you can have a dog.
Sam: I do not have a dog yet, but my sister wants me to adopt one. Can we go there now?
Helen: Of course. It is ten minutes away. We can walk, or I can drive you.
Sam: Let us walk. I want to see the neighbourhood.
Helen: Good idea. On the left you can see the park, and the supermarket is at the end of the road.
Sam: That is very convenient. What about noise? I need to sleep early.
Helen: This street is quiet at night. The busy road is on the other side of the park.
Sam: Excellent. Is the school nearby? My sister's children visit me often.
Helen: Yes, there is a primary school behind the supermarket. Here we are. Number forty-one.
Sam: It looks older than the first building.
Helen: It is older, but the owner painted it last year. Now please come up.
Sam: Oh, the lift is very small.
Helen: It is small, but it works perfectly. We are on the fifth floor. Here is the door.
Sam: The hall is dark. I do not like dark halls.
Helen: Wait until you see the living room. Here you are.
Sam: Wow. The view is amazing. I can see the whole river.
Helen: This is the best feature of the flat. And the balcony is large enough for two chairs and some plants.
Sam: The bedroom is smaller than in the first flat, but I only need a bed and a desk.
Helen: Exactly. And the kitchen is newer. The owner bought a new cooker and a fridge in March.
Sam: That is a big advantage. How much is the rent?
Helen: Seven hundred and fifty pounds, and the heating is included.
Sam: That is much better. Why is it so cheap?
Helen: The owner is moving abroad, and he wants a reliable tenant. He does not care about the money.
Sam: I see. Are there any problems with the building?
Helen: Only one. The washing machine in the basement is old, and it makes a loud noise.
Sam: I can live with that. I wash my clothes once a week.
Helen: Good. Would you like to take a few more photos?
Sam: Yes, please. My sister wants to see the view. Can I send them to her now?
Helen: Of course. While you do that, I will check the contract.
Sam: Thank you. Oh, she answered already. She says it is the most beautiful flat she has ever seen.
Helen: Then I think you have made your decision.
Sam: Almost. I have one more question. When can I move in?
Helen: The flat is empty now, so you can move in next week if you sign today.
Sam: That is very fast. I need to give notice at my old flat first.
Helen: How long is your notice?
Sam: One month. But my landlord is a kind man. Maybe he will let me leave in two weeks.
Helen: Then we can start the contract on the first of next month. Is that acceptable?
Sam: Yes, that sounds fair. What documents do you need from me?
Helen: I need your passport, a copy of your job contract and a deposit of one month's rent.
Sam: I have the passport and the contract with me. The deposit I can pay by card.
Helen: Perfect. You are well prepared, Mr Parker.
Sam: My sister helped me. She said that a good tenant is always ready.
Helen: She is right. Please sign here and here. And then I will give you the keys.
Sam: Already? That is great. Thank you very much, Miss Hill.
Helen: You are welcome. Congratulations on your new home. Do not forget to adopt that dog.
Sam: Maybe next year. First I need to buy some chairs for the balcony.

focus_sounds.tip_ru: Верхние зубы касаются нижней губы, голос включён; не округляйте губы, как для w.
В конце слога язык поднимается к нёбу, звук твёрдый и глубокий; не смягчайте его как русское «ль».
Лёгкий выдох из горла, без русского «х»: рот открыт, язык расслаблен.

questions.question: Why is the first flat a problem for Sam?
questions.answer: It is on the third floor and has no lift.

questions.question: How much is the rent for the second flat?
What can Sam see from the second flat?
What must Sam pay when he signs?
questions.answer: A deposit of one month's rent.
